## Accessibility audit: Join our newsletter Input: HTML, 9 elements. The audit script ran 38 checks and found 7 problems, all failures and no advisories. This is not a conformance claim: only the checks listed here ran. ### Findings 1. **autocomplete** · SC 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA) · failure Element: `` (line 1) Affects: keyboard, voice control Problem: The field asks for the user's own email but has no autocomplete token, so browsers and assistive tools can't fill it in. Fix: ```diff - + ``` 2. **click-no-keyboard** · SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (A) · failure Element: `

It disappears once the user types and isn't a reliable name for the field. Fix: ```diff - + + ``` 4. **html-lang** · SC 3.1.1 Language of Page (A) · failure Element: `` (line 1) Affects: screen reader Problem: The page has no language set, so a screen reader can't pick the right voice and pronunciation. Fix: ```diff - + ``` 5. **img-alt** · SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (A) · failure Element: `` (line 1) Affects: screen reader Problem: The image has no alt attribute, so a screen reader reads out the file name. Fix: ```diff - + ``` If the image is only decorative, use `alt=""` instead. 6. **main-landmark** · SC 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A) · failure Element: `` (line 1) Affects: keyboard, screen reader Problem: The page has no main landmark, so keyboard and screen reader users can't jump straight to the content. ``` 7. **page-title** · SC 2.4.2 Page Titled (A) · failure Element: `` (line 1) Affects: screen reader Problem: The page has no title element, so the browser tab, the history and screen readers have no name for the page. Fix: ```diff - + Join our newsletter - Site name ``` ### Needs a manual test - **Keyboard only:** press Tab through the whole page. Every control should be reachable, the order should follow the reading order, and focus should never get stuck (SC 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3). - **Screen reader** (for example NVDA with Firefox, or VoiceOver with Safari): names, roles, states and headings should be spoken as expected (SC 4.1.2, 1.3.1). - **Voice control** (for example Voice Control or Dragon): saying each visible label should activate its control (SC 2.5.3). - **Zoom and reflow:** at 200%, and at 400% on a 1280 CSS px wide window (about 320 CSS px), no content should be lost and nothing should need scrolling in two directions (SC 1.4.4, 1.4.10). - **Alt text quality:** the script only checks that alt text exists. A person needs to check that it says what the image is for (SC 1.1.1). - **Forms:** submit with errors. A screen reader should announce each error, and focus should move to the first one (SC 3.3.1, 4.1.3). ### Not checked here - Contrast, focus-ring style, spacing and target size: not checked here. The ui-polish skill covers them. - Whether the flow makes sense and whether the words are clear: not part of this audit. ### Open questions - **Finding 5:** what does `banner.jpg` show, or is it purely decorative? Tell me and I'll write the alt text, or use `alt=""` if it's decorative. - **Finding 7:** what is the site name for the title? - **Finding 4:** I assumed `lang="en"` because the page text is English. Change it if the site uses another language.
